blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Delete action is a clickable div, unreachable by keyboard) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-accessibility-2 (Icon-only delete control has no accessible name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Render the delete action as a native `<button type="button" onClick={onDelete}>`. As a `div` with only `onClick`, it has no role, is not in the tab order and does not react to Enter or Space, so keyboard and screen reader users cannot delete a document — the very task the proposal adds. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: Delete action is a clickable div, unreachable by keyboard

findings.recommendation: Give the control a name, e.g. `<button type="button" aria-label="Delete document">`. Its only content is `TrashIcon`, whose `<svg>` is `aria-hidden="true"` (src/components/icons.tsx:3) and has no title, so screen reader users hear nothing that says what the control does. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: Icon-only delete control has no accessible name

findings.recommendation: Add a text alternative: `alt` naming the owner (e.g. `alt={ownerName}`, which needs the owner's name as a prop) since the proposal presents the avatar as showing the owner, or `alt=""` if the name is shown in text elsewhere. Without `alt`, screen readers announce the image file name or URL. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
findings.title: Owner avatar image has no alt attribute

findings.recommendation: Ensure the `icon-button` hit area is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (padding around the 16×16 icon from src/components/icons.tsx:3). The `icon-button` styles were not found in the diff, so the actual size could not be verified. WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
findings.title: Delete target likely smaller than 24×24 CSS pixels
